logline: A villager kid lives behind a 40-block wall that old Tomas raises every morning, and climbs it to see what's out there.
question: why tf is the village wall forty blocks high with no gate?
premise: A plains village sits inside a stone-brick wall 40 blocks high with no gate. Every dawn a little dirt pokes over the rim from outside, and old Tomas, the mason, climbs up and builds one block higher above it. A block of the wall once vanished; Tomas patched it by noon. Tomas is the only one who has been outside: he came in an old minecart before the wall, and he hides when the kids push it. He says there's nothing out there 'we want to trade with'.
twist: The thing outside is a player. The dirt is his pillar (he towers up every morning to look in), the vanished block is the one he mined to peek, the minecart is how players move villagers, and outside the wall is his trading hall: a hundred villagers, each boxed in a one-block cell. The kid reads every clue innocently (a brown plant, blocks that vanish, Tomas good at hide and seek) and climbs to see a monster; he finds 'another village' where everybody gets their own room, and the one person not in a room looks up. The wall was never for monsters; it's for us.

lines.text: The WALL / around my village / is FORTY blocks high.
lines.say: The wall around my village is forty blocks HIGH.
lines.note: one bright breath, proud, like it's the biggest thing in the world

lines.text: Old TOMAS adds / ONE more / every MORNING.
lines.say: Old Tomas adds one more every MORNING.

lines.text: A ZOMBIE / can't even jump / TWO blocks. / So we're SUPER safe!
lines.say: A zombie can't even jump two blocks. So we're super SAFE!
lines.note: delighted, doing the maths, totally sure

lines.text: There's no GATE. / Who NEEDS one? / Everything's IN here.
lines.say: There's no gate. Who needs one? Everything's in HERE.

lines.text: Once, a BLOCK / just VANISHED. / Blocks DO that, / I guess. / Tomas had it BACK / by NOON.
lines.say: Once, a block just vanished. Blocks do that, I guess. Tomas had it back by NOON.
lines.note: a shrug on the middle part, then proud of Tomas

lines.direction: slow and low, his hand still on the patched block

lines.text: Every MORNING, / something BROWN / grows over the TOP. / Like a little PLANT!
lines.say: Every morning, something brown grows over the top. Like a little PLANT!
lines.note: charmed by it, a fun fact; the kid never says dirt (the picture shows it)

lines.text: So old Tomas / climbs up / and builds one HIGHER. / He ALWAYS wins.
lines.say: So old Tomas climbs up and builds one higher. He always WINS.
lines.note: proud, like it's a game Tomas plays with the plant

lines.text: Tomas came here / in that old MINECART. / Like a KING!
lines.say: Tomas came here in that old minecart. Like a KING!
lines.note: impressed, the coolest fact about him

lines.text: When the kids PUSH it, / Tomas runs and HIDES. / He's the BEST / at hide and SEEK.
lines.say: When the kids push it, Tomas runs and hides. He's the best at hide and SEEK.

lines.text: I ASKED him / what's OUT there.
lines.say: I asked him what's out THERE.

lines.text: Nothing we want / to TRADE with.
lines.say: Nothing we want to TRADE with.
lines.direction: old and slow, closing the subject, kind but final

lines.text: So before the SUN came up, / I climbed his LADDER. / I wanted to SEE / a real MONSTER!
lines.say: So before the sun came up, I climbed his ladder. I wanted to see a real MONSTER!
lines.note: sneaky and thrilled, speeding up as he climbs; excited, never scared

lines.text: Outside was / ANOTHER village! / A HUNDRED of us! / EVERYBODY gets / their own ROOM!
lines.say: Outside was another VILLAGE! A hundred of US! Everybody gets their own ROOM!
lines.note: pure delight, the happiest he's been; he thinks it's wonderful

lines.text: Then SOMEONE / not in a ROOM / looked UP.
lines.say: Then someone not in a room looked UP.
lines.note: still bright and curious, a new person to meet; full voice to the end
